text:
rachel: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change in #kernel-opt (merged today) we're seeing an odd perf regression for KV cache lookups in our TP+PP 8-GPU runs. p50 fine, but tail/bandwidth drops on generation heavy workloads. anyone else?

mike: saw that on CI. p99 tokens/sec down ~18% on the 8xA100 baseline when using `int8-qat-kern` fallback. local flamegraphs point at NCCL all-reduce wait spikes during KV gather.

sasha: can you paste the profile snippet? is this during attention KV gather or during output head matmul?

mike: paste from perf-run: 
```
# timeline excerpt (nvprof-like sampling)
0.000s compute matmul_kv (GPU0)
0.002s cudaMemcpy async (KV index)
0.003s ncclAllReduce (KV meta) wait 1.2ms
0.006s matmul_v (GPU0) compute 0.8ms
0.007s stall waiting on nccl 0.9ms
```
Looks like peek overlap but not enough to hide nccl cost.

rachel: important context — this workload uses KV cache sharded by TP slices (tensor parallel per-layer sharding) with PP stage boundaries colocated on GPUs 0/4. So some KV entries require cross-GPU fetch + all-reduce of meta.

anya: earlier hybrid approach (we called it "cache-mesh" in experiments) replicated hot-prefix buckets across PP boundary and reduced nccl frequency. Could that help? tradeoff was memory pressure + slight fp32 activation bump.

mike: memory headroom on 8xA100 is ~14GB free per GPU in these runs. Replicating top-5% hot buckets might be doable. I ran a quick sim: replicating top 3% reduced nccl calls by ~40% and p99 improved ~12%.

bench-bot: automated-bench: run 2026-01-18-08:30: metrics attached -> throughput: baseline 120 tok/s, after-replicate 134 tok/s, tail-latency 95th 11ms -> 9.6ms.

sasha: question: is the dominant cost the all-reduce on KV indices or the subsequent scatter/gather? If all-reduce is the hotspot we should consider switching to reduce-scatter + local gather pattern to lower cross-GPU footprint.

rachel: profile shows both. All-reduce on small meta tensors (keys occupancy) is frequent; then we do an ncclAllGather for actual values in some layers (legacy fallthrough).

anya: idea: change kernel-selection to favor a fused gather+matmul kernel when sequence length < 256 and batch small. That reduces the separate nccl sync points (fuse local fetch with compute). But that's a bigger kernel patch.

mike: the kernel change earlier inadvertently disabled the fused gather path for int8-qat-kern; that's probably why we saw regression. revert candidate: re-enable fused path for int8 with a slowpath for alignment mismatch.

sasha: longer-term, consider hybrid sharding: TP for KV shards inside a PP stage but DP replicate the read-only prefix index across PP boundaries for recent context. That keeps write path consistent (only primary owner updates) but lets reads avoid nccl most of the time.

rachel: can we estimate cost? assume 8 GPUs, 24B model, prefix hot fraction 2% -> replication memory = ~0.02 * total_kv_size. Anyone have numbers?

mike: total_kv_size in test is ~40GB across GPUs -> 2% = 0.8GB -> per-GPU extra 0.8GB if fully replicated. So cheap. The problem is the number of hot buckets changes with prompt distribution; we need eviction policies.

bench-bot: sim-evict: LRU + frequency threshold gave stable mem footprint across traces.

anya: also: batching heuristics matter. When we batch very aggressively we increase sequence-length variance in a batch which increases cross-GPU KV hits. Maybe dynamic batch splitting by prefix-locality would help (group requests that share prefix shards).

sasha: yep. Workload-aware batching: route requests to mini-batches by shard affinity before packing into runtime batch. That preserves throughput and reduces nccl frequency. Could be an ops-level change mostly.

mike: quick config prototype for hybrid route: 
```
cache:
  shard_strategy: hybrid_mesh
  replicate_hot_fraction: 0.03
  hot_selection: lfu_window=10000
  batch_affinity_grouping: true
```
Would need runtime routing hooks and a fallback for cold keys.

rachel: immediate action items: 1) mike — revert the fused-kernel disable for int8 (or add slowpath) and run CI perf suite; 2) sasha — prototype reduce-scatter + local gather in a toy PP topology; 3) anya — add quick sim for replicate_hot_fraction 1/3/5% with current prompts.

anya: ack — will run sims today and share numbers.

mike: starting revert PR now, will link in thread.

sasha: I'll take the small toy change — should be able to measure nccl traffic delta.

rachel: thanks all. if we can get p99 back to within 5% of baseline that's priority for next deploy. adding follow-ups to eng-runtime board. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: deploy-bench queued: perf/regression-check-1832109876, notifications on completion.
